study: Sector lead-lag: when a sector ETF makes a sector-specific move up, do its members that have not moved yet (laggards) catch up over the next 10 minutes by more than the spread?
registered_at: 2026-10-14 premarket (~06:00 ET), before any bar for this study was fetched or any return computed.
origin: docs/PLAN_2026-10-14.md stage 1, idea 3 (operator 10/14: 'test it'). A causal discovery rule: it seats a name before its own move, from a move it can see in its sector.
prior: Weak. tools/studies/sector_study.py (9/14-9/23, book names, 8 days) found sector strength did not predict runway (memory runway-is-findable-profit-is-not-yet); that tested sector strength as a gate on names already seated, not lead-lag across a universe. Intraday sector lead-lag in liquid US names is widely arbitraged.

universe.names: Every symbol on the board (decision_ledger watch/arm rows) on at least 3 of the 26 cached sessions 2026-09-08..2026-10-13 - names the desk's screens recur on, scored on ALL 26 sessions, including days they were not on the board. Requiring 3+ days weakens, but does not remove, selection on a single day's move (caveat).
universe.sector: Finnhub /stock/profile2 finnhubIndustry (ai_reports/industry_cache.json, extended for missing names) mapped to one of SMH, XLK, XLC, XLV, XLF, XLE, XLU, XLRE, XLY, XLP, XLI, XLB by tools/studies/sector_study.MAP (first match). Unmapped names are excluded and counted.
universe.per_day_filters: Prior session close >= $10 and 20-session mean dollar volume >= $20M (SIP daily bars, split-adjusted; minute prices raw). Unknown = excluded, counted.

signal.feed: Detected on IEX 1-minute bars (what the live desk can see): the last IEX close at or before a minute, looking back at most 15 minutes. Outcomes on SIP.
signal.sector_move: At minute m (09:50-15:20 ET): ETF IEX close(m) / close(m-5) - 1 >= +0.25%, AND that minus SPY's same 5-minute return >= +0.10% (a sector move, not the market).
signal.laggard: A universe member mapped to that ETF whose own IEX close(m) / close(m-5) - 1 <= +0.05% and >= -0.50% (has not moved, and is not falling apart).
signal.fire: Each laggard at each qualifying m. 30-minute refractory per symbol (the first fire wins).

outcome: Gross 10-minute markout: SIP close of minute m+10 / SIP open of minute m+1 - 1 (early_entry_honest.markout).
cost: 10 bp round trip for the graded net; the pass also needs net > 0 at 20 bp.
statistic: Day-equal mean of per-day mean net, day-clustered t.
split: Half A = 2026-09-08..09-24, half B = 09-25..10-13 (the same calendar split as the early-entry and board-name studies).
pass: PASS only if in BOTH halves: day-equal net at 10 bp > 0 with t >= 2.0, day-equal net at 20 bp > 0, >= 100 fires and >= 10 sessions with a fire. Short = UNDERPOWERED (no evidence either way); any FAIL half = FAIL. One graded rule.
information_only: lift vs a later same-name minute (entry+1..+60; the null-calibrated control from early_entry_honest)
lift vs the sector's LEADERS at the same minute (members up >= +0.50% over the same 5 minutes): do laggards beat names that already moved?
lift vs the sector ETF's own next 10 minutes (did the laggard just carry sector beta?)
SIP-detected version of the same rule (not computable live)
drops: unmapped, under $10, ADV unknown/low, missing bars, rate-limited fetches
data_integrity: Fetches run after 16:15 ET only, throttled, back off on 429, and never cache a day with a failed chunk. Scoring aborts if more than 5% of universe name-days lack bars or ADV.
no_retuning: +0.25% / +0.10% / +0.05% / -0.50% thresholds, 5-minute window, 30-minute refractory, 10-minute hold, the universe rule and the cost are fixed.
if_pass: Provisional: repeat on >= 10 forward sessions, then a result-skeptic review of the positive, then a live seating design (sector ETFs on the real-time stream).
if_fail: Sector lead-lag is closed as a discovery rule on free data.
script: tools/studies/sector_laglead_study.py: --fetch (industries, daily bars, IEX + SIP minute bars; mini, after 16:15), default inventory with no returns, --score after a result-skeptic READY.
